interpretation: Retain baseline: authored forward 1.5 m/s tracking error regresses, 0.49 m/s tracking and yaw tracking regress, reverse 1.5 m/s requires more torque/slip, and a new turn-transition failure appears. Its improved reverse-speed tracking is a tradeoff, not a general improvement.

Baseline has two failures in the same world during forward 1.5 m/s; authored has one failure in a different world 0.44 s after entering positive-yaw command. The comparator counts transition failures even inside the 2 s warmup.
Authored candidate has 1,500 additional optimizer iterations beyond baseline. This compares available engineering candidates; it does not isolate the causal effect of the reference.

Fast candidate also rejected: all five high-speed tracking errors improve 12.6–79.0%, but reverse 1.5 m/s adds one failure, torque squared rises 69.3%, slip rises 62.3%, and low-speed yaw/slip regress. Same realized randomization and evaluator source as baseline.
The fast-reward stage warmstarts authored, so comparison against stock combines the reference, new reward weights and extra optimization. Do not describe it as a reward-only causal ablation.
Selection uses seed 101; 202 and 303 are two planned heldout seeds, with 404 follow-on evaluation being prepared. Correlated timestep counts are not independent trials.
Bumpy finetuning needs a matched selected-flat-versus-bumpy checkpoint comparison on the same Bumpy scenes; a post-training score alone cannot establish improvement.

Existing traces lack full root orientation/position needed for signed torso geometry audit. Prior plane screens on other checkpoint versions cannot certify these artifacts. Bumpy body-distance diagnostics remain unvalidated.

Local class hardware driver adds a second position clamp 0.10 rad inside policy limits. See local-driver-position-limit-audit.json; controller-clamp simulation is not exact physical parity and installed Pi limits are unknown.
